item.title: 1 missing, 4 rushed to hospital after helicopter crashes off Southern California island
item.description: A medevac helicopter crashed off Catalina Island in California with five aboard, leaving one person missing as search and rescue operations continue.
item.content:encoded:
A medevac helicopter crashed into the water off Catalina Island in California on Wednesday night, with one of the five people aboard reported missing and the other four taken to hospitals, according to officials.

The Los Angeles County Fire Department received reports of the crash shortly before 8 p.m.

Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with the fire department dispatching helicopters and divers shortly after learning of the crash.

3 DEAD, 1 HOSPITALIZED AFTER NEWS HELICOPTER CRASHES IN LOS ANGELES COMMERCIAL AREA

The U.S. Coast Guard also responded to the crash.

"I have been informed that a medevac helicopter leaving Catalina Island has crashed shortly after takeoff. L.A. County Fire, Sheriff, Coast Guard, and Avalon Fire are on the scene," Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn said on X. "Search and rescue operations are underway, and I am praying for everyone who was on board."

At least one of the five people aboard the helicopter remains unaccounted for as of late Wednesday night. Two others were transported to hospitals in stable condition and the remaining two were transported in unknown condition, according to KTLA.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said two people were taken to a hospital on Catalina Island, while two others were transported to the Ronald Reagan Medical Center at UCLA.

The fire department said the helicopter's flight plan was unclear, according to CBS LA. Deputies said the helicopter belonged to Reach Air Medical Services.

US NAVY IDENTIFIES SAILOR LOST IN ARABIAN SEA AFTER HELICOPTER'S EMERGENCY WATER LANDING

Flight tracking data showed a Reach Air Medical Services helicopter departing from Oceanside in San Diego County at 6:40 p.m. and landing on Catalina Island at 7:04 p.m.

Reach said it was aware of the incident but could not provide further information.

"Our immediate concern is for the well-being of those involved," a Reach spokesperson said in a statement to CBS LA.

item.title: Arizona sheriff's helicopter crew rescues man stranded atop overturned truck in rapidly rising floodwaters
item.description: Video captures a Maricopa County sheriff's helicopter crew hoisting a man from his overturned truck as flash flooding surged in Tonopah, Arizona.
item.content:encoded:
Dramatic video shows an Arizona sheriff's helicopter crew rescuing a man stranded on top of his overturned truck as rapidly moving floodwaters surrounded the vehicle.

The Maricopa County Sheriff's Office said its Fox 1 aviation crew responded Tuesday morning to a flooded wash in Tonopah, where deputies found the man sitting atop the overturned vehicle with water rushing around him.

Video released by authorities shows the man perched on the truck as muddy floodwaters rush past him.

Because of the dangerous conditions, first responders determined that directly reaching the man was too risky and decided a "hoist rescue" would be the safest option.

TRAGEDY AT SEA LEAVES TEEN STRANDED ON OVERTURNED BOAT FOR NEARLY 3 DAYS IN FRIGID WATERS

The video shows a Fox 1 crew member being lowered to the vehicle to secure the man in a rescue harness before both are hoisted to safety.

The man was taken to the riverbank, where fire personnel were waiting, according to the sheriff's office.

The helicopter's pilot, Rich Dickner, told CBS News that the water was quickly rising around the vehicle.

"We didn't waste much time," Dickner said.

"As opposed to when we first got there, you can see the water line on the video — it's below the window — and it had risen up to the top of the window," he continued. "So there was that urgency."

HELICOPTER RESCUE CREW CAUGHT ON CAMERA SAVING 2 CLIMBERS TRAPPED ALONG POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH CLIFF

People Magazine reported that Deputy Lindsey Smith was lowered approximately 80 feet from the helicopter toward the overturned truck.

She initially struggled to get her footing before securing herself to the vehicle, according to the report.

The entire rescue took less than five minutes, authorities said.

The Maricopa County Sheriff's Office credited the crew's swift response with getting the man to safety.

"Thanks to the skill and quick response of our Aviation crew, the subject was safely brought to shore," the sheriff's office said.

"Excellent work, Fox 1!"

DEADLY GRAND CANYON FLOODING KNOCKS OUT CRITICAL WATER LINE AMID RACE TO FIND MISSING HIKERS

The Weather Channel reported that remnants of Hurricane Polo brought historic rainfall to parts of the Desert Southwest, contributing to dangerous flash flooding.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County warned drivers not to attempt to cross flooded roads.

"Remember: Conditions can change fast. If you encounter a flooded roadway, Turn Around, Don't Drown."

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office for additional information.

item.title: White Sox, Yankees advance to next round with sweeps as Munetaka Murakami provides quote of the year
item.description: The New York Yankees swept Boston in the Major League Baseball playoffs as Cody Bellinger's three-run blast blew the game open in the sixth inning.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday afternoon had plenty of potential for drama, with all four wild card series offering the potential for teams to advance into the division round of the Major League Baseball playoffs.

The first game of the quadruple-header, the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies, delivered in spades. A Bryce Harper misplay in the 7th inning allowed two Braves' runs to score, putting the Phillies on the brink of elimination. But Schwarber and Harper hit back-to-back homers in the 8th to tie it, and a 10th inning homer for Alec Bohm won it for Philadelphia to force a winner-take-all game three on Thursday.

Then there's the Houston Astros. The Astros entered game two needing a win to force a game three, sending their ace, Hunter Brown, to the mound against the White Sox' powerful lineup. 36 pitches, five hits, four runs, two errors and just two outs later, the White Sox had a 4-0 lead and Brown was out of the game.

YANKEES BULLPEN CATCHER HEAD BUTTS BEN RICE'S GRAND SLAM ON THE FLY IN HILARIOUS MOMENT AGAINST RED SOX

That summed up Houston's series; just not quite good enough to overcome Chicago's offense. The White Sox, one of baseball's most strikeout-prone offenses, had 13 in Wednesday's game, but kept chipping away, fending off an attempted Astros comeback with a massive three-run homer from Chase Meidroth in the 6th inning to give them some breathing room.

Four combined innings from Jordan Hicks and Erick Fedde closed it out to send the White Sox through for a massive ALDS against their division rival Cleveland Guardians. But they weren't done with the entertainment quite yet.

In the postgame clubhouse celebrations, star first year third baseman Munetaka Murakami gave what might be the quote of the season. When asked how he felt, Murakami answered, "100."

A minute later, after being joined by another member of the White Sox staff, Murakami, covered in beer, added, "I'm drunk, I'm drunk. Yesterday, maybe hungover, you know?"

After the interviewer offered a gentle correction, he said, "No, not yesterday, tomorrow. Sorry, I don't speak English."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Impossible not to root for him.

Meanwhile, on the other side of the American League postseason bracket, the New York Yankees had an opportunity to sweep the hated Boston Red Sox after a dominant 9-0 win in game one. And after Cam Schlittler's remarkable outing on Tuesday, Max Fried was nearly as good on Wednesday.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Six innings with just one run allowed, three hits, one walk and six strikeouts, enough for New York to take a 2-1 lead into the bottom of the sixth. Which is where everything imploded for Boston. Garrett Crochet, making his first appearance on a big league mound since late-April, took over, hoping to keep the Yankees at two.

Instead, Spencer Jones reached on a strikeout, then stole second and advanced to third on a throwing error from catcher Adley Rutschmann. George Lombard singled in a run, Jazz Chisholm poked one through the right side, Trent Grisham got a bunt down for a hit, knocking Crochet out of the game without getting an out. Garrett Whitlock came in to stop the bleeding, but after two more runs scored on a sac fly and groundout, Cody Bellinger delivered the big blow.

On a 1-0 changeup, Bellinger took advantage of the short right field porch and knocked in three to make it 8-1.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

New York cruised home with a 9-2 win, setting up an ALDS matchup with the Tampa Bay Rays.

There are a few big takeaways from these two sweeps, namely the importance of power in October baseball. It's an old adage that small ball wins against quality pitching, but it was the homers from Chicago in game one and two that gave them the edge, while Bellinger's bomb effectively put the game out of reach in the Bronx. Even without Aaron Judge, the Yankees' lineup outscored Boston 17-2. And with two days off before the start of the ALDS, Schlittler will be able to start in game two of the ALDS, with Gerrit Cole or Carlos Rodon available for game one.

While the Yankees are through, the other three teams left in the AL bracket are the Guardians, Rays and White Sox. Those teams rank 25th, 26th and 28th in total payroll respectively. There's a long ways to go to reach or win the World Series, but it's a bit of a tough look for MLB that the league office has spent the past few months preparing to lock players out by claiming that small market teams with low payrolls have no hope of meaningful baseball.

Pretty sure those three organizations should have hope. Saturday in Cleveland and Tampa should be a blast. Playoff baseball always is.

item.title: Atlanta Dream advance to WNBA playoffs semifinals for first time since 2018 with Game 2 win
item.description: Angel Reese, Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray powered the Atlanta Dream past Washington as a key third-quarter run decided the WNBA playoffs matchup.
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Dream avoided a first-round playoff exit for the first time in four years.

Atlanta, which finished with the Eastern Conference’s best regular-season record, had little trouble dispatching the Washington Mystics in Game 2 of their first-round WNBA playoff series Tuesday night. Star guard Allisha Gray led the Dream with 22 points in the 83-75 victory, punching Atlanta’s ticket to the semifinals for the first time since 2018.

Atlanta’s postseason run will continue Sunday, when the Dream host Game 1 of the semifinals against New York. The Liberty made league history by sweeping Minnesota, becoming the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in the league's 30-year history.

NEW YORK LIBERTY VS ATLANTA DREAM PREVIEW: WHY THE INTERIOR MATCHUP COULD DECIDE THIS WNBA SHOWDOWN

Jordin Canada made 3-pointers on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, and she added a jumper from the free-throw line on Atlanta’s next trip for an 89-70 lead with just under three minutes left on the clock.

Rhyne Howard, the top pick in the 2022 WNBA Draft, ended the night with 15 points before fouling out with just over six minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. Angel Reese also had 15 points and seven rebounds.

CAITLIN CLARK SAYS SHE AND ANGEL REESE HAVE 'ALWAYS BEEN FRIENDS' AFTER WINNING FIBA WOMEN'S WORLD CUP

The Mystics committed 11 first-half turnovers.

Washington went on a 14-2 run starting in the third quarter to get within 65-62. But Atlanta scored the next 13 points, capped by a 3-pointer by Canada, to rebuild a double-digit lead at 78-62.

The Mystics were making their first playoff appearance since winning the 2019 WNBA championship, while the Dream have captured the conference title three times from 2010-13 but have never won a WNBA championship.

The Dallas Wings hosted the Golden State Valkyries in Wednesday's other first-round series matchup.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Pete Davidson calls out NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani over highway mess
item.description: Pete Davidson called out NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" over the BQE's endless construction to thunderous studio applause.
item.content:encoded:
Pete Davidson didn’t hold back while delivering a blunt message to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

On Monday night, the 32-year-old comedian appeared on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" where Kimmel, 58, told him that Mamdani, 34, would be his next guest. The late night host then pointed out that Davidson was a "lifelong resident of this city" and asked if he had any questions for the mayor.

"Yes, could he fix the "f-----g BQE, please?" Davidson said in a clip shared on the show's Instagram page.

NYC DRIVERS SHELL OUT $9 CONGESTION TOLL. CITY ADMITS IT FAILED TO IMPROVE AIR QUALITY

The BQE, short for the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway, is a major New York City highway that runs through Brooklyn and Queens and has long been criticized for traffic congestion and aging infrastructure.

Davidson's request was immediately met with cheers and thunderous applause from the studio audience.

"You hit on something," Kimmel noted.

"Look at that," Davidson said, gesturing toward the crowd.

"That's the loudest response I've ever gotten," he added with a laugh.

The "Saturday Night Live" star went on to explain that his frustration stemmed from the seemingly endless construction and what he described as a lack of visible work at the site.

MAMDANI'S LATEST FREEBIE SETS OFF ONLINE FURY AS CRITICS RIP CITY PRIORITIES: 'OPERA SOCIALISM'

"The BQE has been under construction since before I was born. And here’s my problem with it," Davidson said. "They’re never doing anything. Someone’s just standing there eating a sandwich or on the phone, and there’s all these cones around."

"So I don't know what mob front or whatever, who's getting money from whatever, but just fix it, please," he added.

ZOHRAN MAMDANI ADMITS HE WANTS TO END HIS ‘ONE-SIDED BEEF’ ABOUT TAXES WITH RAPPER 50 CENT

"I'm going ask him about it. I will ask him about it," Kimmel assured Davidson, who replied, "Yeah, please!"

At the end of Mamdani's appearance on the show, Kimmel presented the mayor with Davidson's question.

"One more thing," Kimmel told Mamdani.

"Hit me," Mamdani said with a smile.

"Pete Davidson wants to know what's going on in the BQE," Kimmel said. "He says he drives by it and he sees nobody doing anything. He said it's been like since before he was born."

Mamdani responded by highlighting his office’s BQE Central Project, a $4 billion plan to rehabilitate the city-owned section of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway between Atlantic Avenue and Sands Street, with construction expected to begin in 2030.

"We're gonna be putting a multi-billion dollar plan to actually repair the part the city owns," Mamdani said. "Which is the part that is currently the most at risk and that's going to be proceeding over the next 10 years. Full safety. No diversion of traffic into local neighborhoods and actually bring it back."

"So you’re saying Pete’s daughter will also be complaining about this," Kimmel joked as Mamdani and the audience laughed.

Fox News Digital reached out to Davidson's and Mamdani's reps for comment.

Mamdani, a Democratic socialist, emerged as a surprise winner in New York City’s mayoral race last November after building a strong following through social media and grassroots campaigning. He took office on Jan. 1 when he was sworn in as mayor.

Davidson has mostly talked about politics jokingly, but he has openly criticized President Donald Trump and supported the Democratic presidential nominee Hillary Clinton during the 2016 election.

After Clinton lost the 2016 election, Davidson posted an angry pro-Clinton message and later got a tattoo of the former Secretary of State, calling her his "hero."

In an interview with Variety that was published Wednesday, Davidson discussed how he is in the process of removing nearly all of his almost 200 tattoos.

"One, they were f----n' horrible," he said of his tattoos. "Two, it was a business decision. I hated coming into the makeup trailer three hours early to spray-paint over horrible f----n' tattoos. And third, I was like, ‘I’m not this dude.’ I got these when I was in an immense amount of pain and I was trying to show people my pain."

Davidson admitted that some of his tattoos were a result of his past struggles with self-harm, saying he initially used the ink to cover scars.

"I used to cut, so some of [the tattoos] covered up the cuts," he told Variety.

However, Davidson confirmed that he would be keeping his Clinton tattoo despite removing most of his other ink.

"She stays," he said of the tattoo depicting Clinton in a power suit on his right leg.

"That’s my dog," Davidson added of Clinton. "I love Hillary, man. She’s awesome and a good friend."

item.title: Netanyahu praises heroic bystander in bloody cockpit attack for preventing ‘another 9/11’
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised the heroic passenger who stormed the cockpit as the FlyDubai plane plunged 13,000 feet in one minute.
item.content:encoded:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the bloody cockpit attack that occurred on a flight headed from Dubai to Tel Aviv during an exclusive interview with Fox News on Wednesday.

Netanyahu recounted how the event unfolded and praised the "unbelievable courage" of passengers who quickly corralled the alleged attacker and stabilized the plane, specially crediting Yaniv Chayon, the man who broke into the cockpit and tamed the attacker.

The prime minister said he prevented the world from a disaster of "unbelievable proportions."

"The passengers, including 30 children, are already saying their prayers. They know they're gone from this world," he told "Hannity." "And this young man just acts with incredible, incredible heroism and saves the day."

FLYDUBAI PILOT STABS FELLOW PILOT, ATTEMPTS TO CRASH PLANE, NETANYAHU SAYS

"He acted with coolness of judgment and heroism… just tremendous courage that prevented another 9/11."

The 9/11 terrorist attacks killed nearly 3,000 people.

MIKE PENCE: REMEMBER THE FALLEN — AND THE GENERATION THAT DEFENDED AMERICA SINCE 9/11

A pilot aboard the Israel-bound FlyDubai flight allegedly stabbed another pilot and apparently attempted to "crash the plane" with more than 100 people onboard — an incident authorities describe as a suspected hijacking.

The wounded captain unlocked the cockpit door, letting in passengers who worked together to subdue the attacker and stabilize the nosediving aircraft.

UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT

Netanyahu met with Chayon earlier on Wednesday, lauding his act of courage and praising him for taking control of the plane under "impossible" circumstances.

"I met with this Israeli, this unbelievable Israeli. His name is Yaniv, who did this thing," he explained. "And I asked him, ‘How did you do it?’ And he said, ‘Well, I just had to do it.’"

MIDAIR BRAWL ERUPTS ON PACKED FLIGHT AS SCREAMING PASSENGERS JUMP FROM SEATS

"His family was there, 174 passengers, most of whom were Israelis, were there. He had to save them."

Netanyahu blamed "hatred" for the attack and said it was rooted in antisemitism and that many have "fallen prey" to what he described as "propaganda" that vilifies Israel.

ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS

"I don't know the exact background of this person, the attacker, but he obviously hated Israelis because he was going to kill about 170 of them on this plane, killing himself, too," the prime minister said.

"That's fanaticism and hatred of an incalculable level."

While the captain was incapacitated, the aircraft dropped from 30,000 feet to 17,000 in roughly one minute before it diverted to Saudi Arabia, according to flight radar. Other pilots aboard the aircraft took control and landed it safely.

The pilot of Flight 1073 has been identified as Capt. Smit Machchhar. Netanyahu says he is "fighting for his life" after sustaining severe injuries.

PLANE PASSENGERS SCREAM IN HARROWING MID-FLIGHT VIDEO AS VIOLENT SHAKING SENDS CABIN CEILING PANELS FLYING

"Apparently, he stabbed him, or he hit him with an ax. He was bleeding profusely. The plane began to go out of control and began a nosedive," Netanyahu said.

"The pilot who was there was an Indian pilot with sort of a very badly wounded. He's fighting, I think, for his life right now, but in an act of unbelievable courage, he managed to unlock the door to the cockpit."

AMERICANS WARNED AGAIN TO RETHINK TRAVEL AS MISSILE ATTACK RATTLES HISTORIC REGION

Netanyahu told Reuters that the alleged cockpit attacker was arrested after the plane made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. An Israeli official identified the co-pilot as an Omani national.

FlyDubai cautioned that the suspect’s motive remains unknown and declared that all flights in and out of Israel will be suspended while the investigation is carried out.

Israeli officials say investigators are working to examine the co-pilot’s motive and whether he acted alone.

"Just think about it... If you're next hijacked, make sure an Israeli is sitting next to you," Netanyahu said.

item.title: TikTok couple charged with arson after house fire causes $10K in damage
item.description: Dakota Harper and Felicity Eatmon face arson and conspiracy charges after a fire damaged an abandoned home and nearby church.
item.content:encoded:
A TikTok couple was arrested Tuesday for allegedly setting an abandoned West Virginia home on fire, possibly causing more than $10,000 in damage to a nearby church.

Dakota Harper, 21, and Felicity Eatmon, 22, were each charged with first-degree arson and one count of conspiring to commit an offense that carries a potential life sentence, according to the Kanawha County Magistrate Court.

The pair is known for posting videos together on social media and have amassed 28,000 followers on TikTok.

SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCER PLEADS GUILTY AFTER PRANK VIDEOS AT ARIZONA CHIPOTLE, OTHER BUSINESSES

A video showing Harper at his arraignment has since gone viral for highlighting his stature. According to court records, Harper stands at 3-foot, 9-inch height and weighs 43-pounds.

At the Kanawha County courtroom, Harper took a seat before an officer approached from behind and tucked his chair closer to the table, leaving his head barely above the desk.

Eatmon, who referred to herself as Harper’s fiancée in their social media videos, also appeared alongside him. She stands at 5 feet, 1 inch tall, records indicated.

According to WCHS-TV, the fire was reported at 11:15 p.m. Sunday in the West Side of Charleston.

SURVEILLANCE VIDEO SHOWS OFFICERS TACKLE 'ANTI-AMERICAN' SUSPECT AFTER FEDERAL BUILDING FIREBOMBING

Surveillance footage captured Eatmon giving Harper what appeared to be a piece of paper that was then lit on fire and placed inside the home, the outlet reported, citing a complaint.

Investigators reportedly said the home was abandoned and had no active utilities. The remains continued to smolder into Monday morning.

The adjacent Canaan United Methodist Church sustained significant damage as a result of the blaze, according to the complaint.

Both suspects are currently being held on a $10,000 bond each.

item.title: Actress Monet Mazur's $1.5M Hollywood Hills home targeted by masked suspects in break-in attempt
item.description: "All-American" actress Monet Mazur's Hollywood Hills home was the target of an invasion. Police responded to a "hot prowl burglary" radio call.
item.content:encoded:
Monet Mazur's Hollywood Hills property was the target of a home invasion Saturday, Fox News Digital confirmed.

Los Angeles Police Department officers responded to a "hot prowl burglary" radio call before 11:30 p.m. with the suspects reportedly still at the location, officials told Fox News Digital.

"At least one victim was inside the residence when the suspects attempted to gain entry," authorities said. "The suspects fled the scene before officers arrived."

SUSPECT ARRESTED AT KIM KARDASHIAN'S MANSION AFTER STOLEN VEHICLE, BREAK-IN REPORTED IN HIDDEN HILLS

The "All-American" actress reportedly spotted three people on security cameras who were dressed in black clothing and wearing ski masks, according to the Post.

The outlet claimed Mazur, 50, "confronted" the suspects before they entered her home, which then prompted them to flee.

HGTV STARS TAREK AND HEATHER EL MOUSSA FEEL 'VIOLATED' AFTER BURGLARS RANSACK NEWPORT BEACH HOME

Images obtained from the property appeared to show pepper spray "visible on the doormat outside" of the two-bedroom, $1.5 million property, The Post claimed.

TMZ, however, reported that the actress's alarm was triggered by the suspects when they allegedly tried to open her front door, which prompted them to run off, noting that no one confronted them and nothing was taken.

"Officers searched the location; however, they did not locate any suspects," officials told Fox News Digital. "No suspect description is available at this time. No injuries were reported, and officers completed a burglary report."

Mazur's representatives did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Last month, Olympian Simone Biles told TikTok followers her Chicago home was robbed earlier this year after three suspects allegedly stole her Porsche GTS, which was later recovered by authorities.

EAGLES STAR SAQUON BARKLEY'S HOME BURGLARIZED, POLICE SAY

Biles told followers about the "absolute insanity" surrounding the theft, and admitted she debated sharing more with followers in an upcoming "storytime."

In response to the intrusion, Biles, 29, and husband Jonathan Owens increased their home security by acquiring a Doberman Pinscher.

After another celebrity residence was targeted by suspects, U.S. Army veteran Stephen Scott, founder of Scott's K9, told Fox News Digital professionally trained protection dogs can provide an added layer of defense for homeowners.

"A protection dog in a situation of a home break-in, they're gonna hear way before you, they're gonna smell way before you," Scott said.

"The biggest thing that they're going to do is they're going to buy you a lot of time."

Scott noted that a trained K-9 will "start barking" at the sight and sound of an intruder and essentially provide more time for an owner to assess any situation.

WATCH: EXPERT EXPLAINS HOW PROTECTION DOGS CAN HELP DURING A BREAK-IN

"They're gonna go to where the person's coming through the door," he said. "It's gonna give you a chance to grab the kids, grab a gun, or call 911 ... these dogs definitely buy you a sense of time."

When questioning a particular vulnerability some homeowners may have, Scott noted digital footprints can add to unnecessary access.

"They post everything online when they're gone from the house, what time, what their schedule is," he said. "'Oh, going to drop Joey off at school at 7:45. Gotta go back, go on an errand.'

"That's probably the biggest thing that we've seen an increase in is just online and everyone posting a picture of where they're at. Everyone knows when they're gone."

item.title: Patrick McEnroe on U.S. Open weed smell, trans athletes, foreign recruits reshaping college tennis
item.description: Patrick McEnroe is taking his fight over foreign recruits in college tennis to Capitol Hill, backing a new bill heading before the House now.
item.content:encoded:
Tennis icon Patrick McEnroe is pushing for federal reform in college athletics while weighing in on transgender participation and the mysterious weed stench that hit the U.S. Open this year.

Appearing on OutKick's "Tomi Lahren is Fearless," the former U.S. Davis Cup captain sounded the alarm on foreign recruits dominating American college rosters, calling tennis the ultimate "canary in the coal mine." Watching a marquee matchup between top SEC and ACC teams, McEnroe noticed a staggering imbalance: 21 of the 24 players on court were foreign recruits.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

McEnroe stressed, "So I knew that the numbers were getting pretty high in tennis. I've been in tennis my whole life. I played college tennis, had an amazing experience, and I became, quite frankly, deeply concerned."

McEnroe is taking a stand in order to award the most opportunities possible to American collegiate athletes. The response prompted McEnroe to pen a Wall Street Journal op-ed and take his fight straight to Capitol Hill, meeting with Washington politicians to push a new bill currently heading before the House of Representatives.

SENATE MOVES TO REIN IN COLLEGE SPORTS 'WILD WEST' WITH SWEEPING NEW RULES FOR PLAYERS, SCHOOLS

"American universities were put in place, the athletic departments, to help our kids, to educate them, to give them opportunity," McEnroe argued, stressing U.S. schools should prioritize domestic talent over international pros.

McEnroe didn't pull punches on trans athletes in women's sports either. As a father of three daughters, McEnroe wants to protect young girls in sports.

"I'm not for a trans playing in female sports, no, I'm not," McEnroe said.

The veteran broadcaster also weighed in on the marijuana haze that disrupted play at the U.S. Open, urging complaining players to lighten up. McEnroe blamed tournament workers taking quick breaks on the street behind the venue.

TENNIS STAR ARYNA SABALENKA SUPPORTS WTA TRANSGENDER RULES, SAYS MALES SHOULDN'T FACE WOMEN

"Instead of taking a break and having some Gatorade, I guess they were taking a little puff," he joked.

Broadcasting one night with brother John, Patrick admitted he actually misses the old days when charcoal grill smoke drifted over the courts.

COCO GAUFF APPEARS TO SUPPORT WTA EFFORTS TO PROTECT SPORT'S FAIRNESS, LAMENTS 'ATTACK' ON TRANS COMMUNITY

"I kind of miss the smell of the burger," McEnroe laughed. "A little weed, if I smelled it in the air, wouldn't affect me as much as a burger, the smell from the charcoal of the burger."

"Get over it," McEnroe declared. "Making a mountain out of a molehill, not that big of a deal."

item.title: Hasan Piker speaks to UT Austin students after backlash from Texas lawmakers
item.description: Hasan Piker took the stage at UT Austin despite bipartisan backlash from Greg Abbott, Ted Cruz and others, drawing a packed venue of cheering students.
item.content:encoded:
After much scrutiny, controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker spoke to students at the University of Texas in Austin. Sporting a Longhorn orange tie and pin, Piker began the stream in his hotel room and continued it backstage at UT Austin before he finally took the stage.

On Sunday, the University Democrats said they were forced to "return tickets to thousands of students," claiming that UT Austin refused to give them a larger space and an off-campus venue decided it would not host the event after "internal discussions." 

The student group declared it would not cancel the event despite outside pressure to do so.

Piker was welcomed into the event Wednesday evening with loud cheers and applause. The venue looked almost entirely filled. He opened his speech with "Hook 'Em Horns," garnering another wave of cheers. The streamer went on to thank the students for attending the event despite the backlash it received.

CONTROVERSIAL STREAMER HASAN PIKER'S LECTURE AXED BY UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON AMID FREE SPEECH QUESTIONS

"There was supposed to be 3,000 people here today. Three thousand. It's a real testament to how much progress can be made in even a state like Texas that the people in the national Democratic Party have left behind," Piker told the crowd. 

"That's why I wanted to come here today, not just because of the pushback, not in spite of the pushback, but because I know for a fact that there are people who want their voices to be heard."

At the top of his speech, Piker addressed allegations he hates the U.S., saying, "I always tell people that if I hated America, I'd be a Republican." He went on to accuse President Donald Trump of "destroying" the country.

In his remarks, Piker focused much of his ire on Republicans, Trump, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Israel.

The event was hosted by the University Democrats, a student group at UT Austin, and it drew backlash soon after it was announced. Ahead of the event, Texas lawmakers from both sides of the aisle, including Gov. Greg Abbott, Sen. Ted Cruz and Rep. Henry Cuellar condemned Piker's appearance in the Lone Star State.

And Piker condemned all of them at the beginning of his remarks at the university.

HASAN PIKER DOUBLES DOWN, DEFENDS HIS 'GOD-GIVEN RIGHT' TO SAY HOW MUCH HE HATES AMERICA

Cuellar raised concerns on X about Jewish students at UT Austin being made to feel unsafe due to Piker's presence.

The Twitch streamer approached their criticism by speaking about the First Amendment and the importance of freedom of speech. However, he argued that those on the left are not given the same freedom as their ideological counterparts on the right. 

Additionally, Andrew Mahaleris, press secretary for Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, also chimed in, telling Jewish News Syndicate (JNS), "Terrorist sympathizers have no place in Texas."

In a statement provided to Fox News Digital Sept. 16, Cruz said the event was a statement about the status of the Democratic Party.

"Hasan Piker is an America-hating Marxist who has said that America deserved 9/11 and celebrates political violence against Republicans," Cruz's statement said. 

"Americans are entitled to free speech, but it is incumbent upon good people to condemn Piker's incitement. Instead, some Democrats are bringing him to college campuses, while almost all other Democrats are conspicuously silent or worse. It says everything about the state of their party."

In his criticism of the Texas lawmakers, Piker spoke about the First Amendment, claiming that those on the right are often given more freedom than those on the left.

HASAN PIKER POINTS THE FINGER AT AIPAC AS DEMOCRATS SPEAK OUT AGAINST HIM

"I want to talk about the hypocrisy of free speech," Piker said. "It seems to only go in one direction, right? You can't have an opinion that's outside of the permission structure, and the permission structure year over year seems to swing wide in the right direction."

Despite the bipartisan backlash, the event at UT Austin was relatively smooth and proceeded without any major disruptions. After his speech wrapped, Piker thanked the audience on his livestream and admitted that while he was apprehensive about being in Texas, the turnout proved the demand for progressive voices even in a red state.

WOMAN’S ALLEGED ISIS RADICALIZATION UNFOLDED ONLINE BEFORE CAPITOL BOMB PLOT: COURT DOCS

DPS special agents worked alongside the FBI and local law enforcement agencies to investigate the threat.

MUGSHOT OF ACCUSED NY CAPITOL ISIS PLOTTER REVEALED AS FEDS DETAIL PLANS FOR MORE ATTACKS

item.title: Reparations advocates slam cash compensation ‘handout’ label, point to past government remedies
item.description: Reparations advocates demand direct cash payments to descendants of enslaved Americans, warning broader eligibility risks are diluting the movement.
item.content:encoded:
Reparations advocates are insisting that the federal government provide direct cash payments to Black descendants of American slavery, warning that broadening the eligibility scope risks diluting the movement amid growing resistance from conservatives and the Trump administration.

"Cash payments — that’s just a little solution to it, but it’s a big solution because without cash payments, there’s no reparations," Rev. Phyllis Coachman, a supporter of the U.S. Freedmen Project, told Fox News Digital.

"[Slavery] ended in 1865, but so many other things happened after that," Coachman added. "After slavery, the collapse of Reconstruction. We had Jim Crow. We had legal segregation, disenfranchisement. We had lynching

"We had racial terror, destruction of Black property and communities, housing discrimination, redlining, discriminatory lending, barriers to wealth building …. the war on drugs and mass incarceration."

CHAOS ERUPTS AT NY REPARATIONS HEARING AS ‘FOUNDATIONAL’ BLACK AMERICANS CLASH WITH LEFT-LEANING GROUPS

The U.S. Freedmen Project, an organization representing self-identified "foundational Black Americans," works to educate the public on the distinctions between Black Americans who are direct descendants of enslaved persons in the U.S. and those who immigrated to the country voluntarily.

According to its official website, the group is a nonpartisan organization seeking to fulfill the abandoned missions of the 19th-century Freedmen’s Bureau and the Freedmen’s Savings and Trust Company. Supporters argue that broader reparations bills risk violating constitutional principles, contending instead that state and federal officials must base eligibility criteria strictly on lineage.

The debate comes as several state and local governments explore reparations initiatives intended to compensate Black residents for historic racial injustice. Evanston, Illinois, a Chicago suburb, became the first U.S. city to offer direct remedies, providing up to $25,000 in homeownership grants and cash payments to eligible Black residents to address legacy housing discrimination.

Reparations advocate Annette Wilcox pushed back against critics who frame direct monetary payouts as government handouts, arguing the term is used selectively to delegitimize Black claims.

"My thoughts about people who say cash payments are handouts is this is a government that has given trillions of dollars to all sorts of people as reparations," Wilcox told Fox News Digital. 

"We have reparations for 9/11. We've had — even things that aren't reparations after the crash and the Depression, there was an estimated $5 trillion in programs, money and remedies given to people — 90% went to White people at that time. So, handouts are, you know, just, frankly, an insult that people give to Black people.

"The government has a responsibility for what it did to the citizens — the Black people who were enslaved in this country — and it needs to own up to it just like it owned up to what it did to the Native Americans, the Japanese and many other groups that it has given reparations to."

SOME BLACK NEW YORKERS DEMAND CASH PAYMENTS AS ONLY 'TRUE' FORM OF JUSTICE

Fox News Digital previously attended a public hearing hosted by the New York State Community Commission on Reparations Remedies at Hempstead High School on Long Island. During the hearing, residents warned panel officials that expanding the definition of reparations to include recent immigrants or other marginalized groups risks co-opting the movement.

The New York commission was established after Gov. Kathy Hochul signed legislation in December 2023 creating a state panel to examine the legacy of slavery in New York and evaluate potential remedies.

Among those who testified in Long Island, U.S. Freedmen movement supporter Aubrey Muhammad called for an explicit payout amount of $800,000 per eligible individual.

"We need $800,000 for each foundational Black American. That's simple," Muhammad told Fox News Digital. "In New York, that's about the cost of living that'll get you a home, a small business, or help you recover from financial duress."

CHICAGO SUBURB LOCALS HOPE REPARATIONS ADDRESSES 'AFFORDABILITY PRESSURES' AS BLACK POPULATION DWINDLES

However, Devine Prince, president of the U.S. Freedmen Project, noted that such figures reflect broader efforts to address the national wealth gap rather than standard baseline figures. Still, Prince maintained that direct compensation remains non-negotiable.

"If you count yourself as a true American, then there should be no pushback and no rebuttals for direct monetary compensation for the harm that was done," Prince said. "That needs to be repaired through direct monetary compensation to American freedmen."

There’s two kinds of eulogies at funerals. One of them is, ‘This is what this guy did.’ The other one is, ‘This is who this guy was.’ When I’m dead, burned up and I’m ashes and I’m in the wind, I know which eulogy I want to have. I know what I want people to say about me at my funeral. I know what I expect from you, Will. After a couple years, I still don’t think anybody sees it, man.

item.title: 'Nobody Wants This': Consulting rabbi calls out star's 'ignorant' take on 'genocide' in Gaza
item.description: Rabbi Steve Leder, a former consulting advisor on Netflix's "Nobody Wants This," called star Adam Brody's Gaza genocide claim "ignorant" and his tone "disgusting."
item.content:encoded:
Rabbi Steve Leder, a technical advisor behind Netflix's "Nobody Wants This," called out the series star Adam Brody on Tuesday for saying he believes Israel is committing "genocide" in Gaza.

"Hi Adam, you might not remember me. My name is Rabbi Steve Leder, and I was the technical advisor for Season 1 of 'Nobody Wants This,'" Leder began in an Instagram video to the actor. 

"My job was to make sure that your character was authentic and that everything in Season 1 about Judaism was authentic."

Leder criticized Brody and called his comments "ignorant," arguing that Brody had mischaracterized the situation in Gaza and treated the issue flippantly. 

BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM

"Your pronouncement the other day about a ‘genocide in Gaza’ was truly shocking," Leder said. "Not only because of your misuse and mischaracterization of your use of the word genocide — there is no genocide in Gaza, there are genocides in other countries happening, but you failed to mention any of them. 

"You, by your own admission, are a relatively ignorant Jew, and your ignorance really showed the other day.

"If you’re going to use a word like ‘genocide,’ you ought to know what it means," he added. "And, by the way, being so flippant about a word like ‘genocide’ — ‘Hey, put me down for genocide,’ like you’re asking for a table for two at Craig’s — is disgusting. Here’s some more technical advice: If you know nothing about something, you should say nothing about it."

Brody, who plays a rabbi in the series, recently suggested in an interview with GQ magazine that Israel is committing "genocide" in Gaza. 

"Put me down as thinking it's a genocide," Brody said. "Put me down as wanting a free Palestine. It's awful that it's taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it's reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago. I'm hopeful that another administration can really do some good and correct some of these policies that are helping that situation be as awful as it is."

Fox News Digital reached out to Brody's representatives for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

RABBINIC GROUP ACCUSES JEWISH ENTERTAINERS OF 'WHITEWASHING ANTISEMITISM' IN MARK RUFFALO DEFENSE

In a comment to Fox News Digital, Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, also called out Brody as "ignorant" for calling Israel's actions in Gaza "genocide."

"One of the hallmarks of antisemitism is to irrationally regard Jews as a threat. While Hamas was holding, torturing, raping and murdering hostages, only a bigot would call the effort to free those hostages ‘genocide.’ An ignorant Jew is no less likely than anyone else to fall prey to hateful indoctrination," Menken said.

"As even photographer Motaz Azaiza now admits, Hamas could have ended the conflict in Gaza at any moment, simply by releasing the hostages," he added. "In no genocide in history have the victims controlled the off switch. On roughly a daily basis, a prominent Jewish leftist goes on X (formerly Twitter) to say ‘As a Jew’ and then follow it by expressing antisemitic nonsense."

MS RACHEL CONFRONTED ON ACCUSING ISRAEL OF 'GENOCIDE' IN PARK INTERACTION WITH PODCASTER

In another comment from the Israeli-American Council, the organization expressed "revulsion at the ignorant and harmful statement" made by Brody.

"Lies like this are not just fake news, they incite violence that can lead to the murder of innocent Jews. Just today, Israeli passengers narrowly escaped death from what is being called an attempted terrorist attack on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. That's the reality Israelis and Jews live with every day," the organization said.

item.content:encoded:
A 21-year-old University of Georgia student survived an eight-story fall from an apartment window after apparently falling through a screen while dancing near an open window, according to a police report obtained by Fox News Digital.

Kristin Sargent fell from an eighth-floor window at the Rambler Athens apartment complex on West Broad Street around 7:37 p.m. Saturday.

Witnesses told police Sargent had been dancing on a couch or air mattress near the open window when she apparently fell through the screen. She landed near a pool in a courtyard on the building's second floor, according to the report.

WOMAN DIES AFTER PLUNGING INTO UNCOVERED MANHOLE OUTSIDE LUXURY STORES

Lt. Katie Jenkins, a spokesperson for the Athens-Clarke County Police Department, told Fox News Digital that investigators believe the bench helped break Sargent's fall. She said the incident is not being investigated as a criminal matter and that police understand Sargent is alert and conscious.

Emergency 911 audio obtained by FOX 5 Atlanta captured the frantic moments after Sargent fell.

"We’re on the eighth floor. My friend just fell out of the window," a caller told dispatchers. "She's on the ground. She fell out of the window. We were dancing, and she just fell out of the window."

A dispatcher asked whether Sargent was moving.

MAN ACCUSED OF LURING UGA STUDENT WITH ‘WALK HOME’ RUSE BEFORE BRUTAL ASSAULT: POLICE

The caller later told the dispatcher she could see Sargent below but could not determine whether her eyes were open.

"No, I don't know. I'm looking down at her on the floor. She's not moving," the caller said.

Emergency responders transported Sargent to a hospital, where police investigators interviewed her and witnesses while forensic personnel investigated, according to the police report.

LAKEN RILEY MURDER EXPOSED GLARING SECURITY LAPSES ON COLLEGE CAMPUSES, NEED FOR EMERGENCY BLUE LIGHTS

A responding officer wrote that information gathered at the time suggested the fall was an accident. Jenkins told Fox News Digital police are not investigating the incident as a criminal matter.

The report identifies Sargent as a resident of the apartment where the fall occurred.

Police could not address the window or what safety measures may or may not have been in place.

Rambler Athens previously said it was reviewing the incident.

Fox News Digital reached out to the apartment complex for additional information about the window and any safety measures in place at the time of the fall.

A representative for the University of Georgia did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for additional information.

item.title: ICE arrests illegal alien accused of sexually assaulting children after Fairfax County release: DHS

item.content:encoded:
A Honduran illegal immigrant facing multiple child sex crime charges is back in federal custody after authorities in Fairfax County, Virginia, released him from an immigration detainer, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested Oscar Evaristo Nunez Sept. 15 during a targeted enforcement operation, DHS announced Wednesday.

Nunez was initially arrested Aug. 27, 2025, on charges of aggravated sexual battery involving children and offenses related to the non-consensual filming of an undressed minor, according to DHS.

ICE lodged a detainer with the Fairfax County Adult Detention Center two days later, but DHS said local authorities did not honor it and released Nunez without notifying the agency.

GUATEMALAN MAN CHARGED WITH CHILD PORN POSSESSION RELEASED BY FAIRFAX COUNTY DESPITE ICE DETAINER, DHS SAYS

The case has become the latest point of contention between the Trump administration and Virginia officials over cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

"Another criminal illegal alien has been taken off the streets by the brave men and women of ICE with no help from sanctuary politicians in Fairfax County," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a news release. 

"This illegal alien from Honduras had been arrested for child sex crimes in August last year, but Fairfax County refused to honor ICE’s detainer and let this creep back out onto the streets.

"Once again, ICE did the job that these heartless sanctuary politicians won’t do: enforce the law and protect American lives. DHS is calling on Gov. Abigail Spanberger and her fellow sanctuary politicians to stop putting the needs of illegal aliens over the safety of the American people."

‘OUT OF CONTROL’ KILLINGS IN SPANBERGER’S VIRGINIA REACH ‘INSANE’ POINT AS MIGRANT CHARGED IN STABBING SPREE

Spanberger, a Democrat, was not governor when Nunez was arrested, and ICE filed the detainer in August 2025. She took office in January 2026.

Spanberger has moved Virginia away from some forms of state participation in federal immigration enforcement since taking office, including directing state agencies to terminate agreements with ICE under the federal 287(g) program.

A representative for Fairfax County did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

DHS said Nunez illegally entered the U.S. near Arizona around September 2003.

Nunez remains in ICE custody pending immigration proceedings.

item.title: Passenger's bizarre use of drinking glass on flight leaves travelers horrified
item.description: Leaving his fellow travelers mortified, an EVA Air business-class passenger was caught on video using a drinking glass to scratch his scalp mid-flight. An etiquette expert weighed in.
item.content:encoded:
An EVA Air business-class passenger left fellow travelers aghast by using a drinking glass to vigorously scratch his scalp while he was seated in the middle of the flight. 

The odd incident aboard a recent flight out of Taiwan on Sept. 24 was all caught on video. 

The man aboard the Boeing 787 Dreamliner apparently decided that the best way to soothe an itchy head was to vigorously massage his scalp using the rim of a drinking glass.

MIDAIR SCARE FORCES PACKED PASSENGER JET INTO EMERGENCY LANDING, TRAVELERS HOSPITALIZED

The bizarre in-seat grooming routine was spotted by a horrified fellow passenger seated directly behind the amateur masseur, according to news outlet Viral Press.

Watching the traveler drag the rim of the upside-down cup through his hair repeatedly and all across his scalp made the witness feel the premium cabin experience had taken a drastic and unexpected turn.

"This is disgusting. It's a cup, not a massage comb," the appalled witness complained.

Losing all appetite for the upcoming meal service, the passenger who recorded the video said, "No one wants to eat your dandruff. I'm really going to vomit," Viral Press reported.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The EVA Air flight landed safely, NewsFlare reported. 

The company, headquartered in Taiwan, was founded in 1989, according to its website. 

Texas-based etiquette expert Diane Gottsman told Fox News Digital that "using a glass to scratch [one's] head is completely inappropriate," particularly while in public and surrounded by other people. 

"Any time you see someone scratching themselves with an object, or even scratching themselves with their fingers in a public area — it’s unappealing and somewhat alarming," she added.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

In recent years, several flyers have complained that fellow passengers are crossing the line when it comes to public-facing behavior aboard planes.

In March 2026, a passenger was slammed for putting feet up on a window.

At the time, a Reddit user blasted the other traveler.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"First time experiencing the feet in my face in five years. Travel monthly. In first class, and this lady put her feet on my arm rest. I shoved them off."

The writer continued, "And five minutes later, she has them up on her window. At least she has socks on. But come on, people! It’s a 4.5 hour flight."

Said Gottsman, "When you’re in your home, you are in a private space. [But] when you are out in public, there are different standards because you are around other people and must be aware of your surroundings and the comfort level of others."

item.title: Anticipation builds as MIke Tomlin prepares to unveil his Minecraft city that's 12 years in the making
item.description: Mike Tomlin reveals he's been secretly building a "Minecraft" city for twelve years, calling it therapeutic during his high-pressure coaching career.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 NFL season is the first without Mike Tomlin somewhere on the sidelines in decades.

And while the former Steelers coach has moved into the world of TV broadcasting, he's about to become a big deal in a corner of the internet no one would've expected a few months ago.

"Minecraft" streaming.

That's right, the longtime Steelers head coach is about to let fans into the blockified city he has been crafting for the last twelve years.

"It was therapeutic for me," Tomlin said in a video posted to social media. "It allowed me to detach from the pressures and the reality of life. Kind of my secret obsession, and so let's take you all through it."

The video then teased the release of a full video on Tomlin's YouTube channel, which showed an aerial view of a city that had a baseball field, streets, and even buildings with what looked to my eye to be HVAC equipment on the roof.

Mike means business, and I love it.

BREAKING UP TROY AIKMAN AND JOE BUCK WOULD BE A BIG MISTAKE FOR ESPN | BOBBY BURACK

The "NBC Sunday Night Football" analyst revealed in an interview around the start of the season that he was a big fan of the building game that has become a cultural phenomenon over the years.

It makes so much sense to me.

RAMS COACH SEAN MCVAY'S '60 MINUTES' INTERVIEW REVEALS WHY YOU SHOULDN'T FIND YOUR IDENTITY IN YOUR JOB

Being an NFL coach is such a high-pressure job with a lot of noise. How better to get a break from that than by focusing all of your attention on the 8-bit stadium you're trying to construct?

I can't think of one, and it's a pretty healthy way to tune everything out and get yourself focused on the present.

If you're wondering how he was able to handle being an NFL coach for so long, well, for twelve of those years, this is your answer.

Now that Tomlin isn't leading an NFL team anymore, he's got more time to devote to Tomlinburg (or whatever he calls it), and I expect it to be looking like Tokyo in a few months.

item.title: California superintendent candidate calls out teachers union after group leader calls her 'real threat'
item.description: Leaked audio captured a teachers union calling Sonja Shaw a "real threat" as the California Teachers Association spends millions backing her opponent.
item.content:encoded:
Conservative California superintendent candidate Sonja Shaw told Fox News Digital Tuesday she would not back down from confronting the United Teachers Los Angeles union (UTLA) after a circulated video allegedly showed a union leader calling Shaw a "real threat" and warning that her election "would cause a huge problem for us."

Shaw, the president of the Chino Valley Unified School District board, pointed to Los Angeles student achievement scores as she accused UTLA of protecting the education establishment rather than focusing on academic outcomes.

"I’m not surprised the Los Angeles teachers union sees me as a threat," Shaw said in a statement to Fox News Digital. 

"More than half of their students still can’t read at grade level, and nearly two-thirds can’t do math. Instead of working to help those kids, UTLA has fought to keep parents in the dark, excused failure and protected the system that produced these results."

NATION’S LARGEST TEACHERS UNION UNDER FIRE AS CONTROVERSIAL AGENDA PUTS CENTURY-OLD FEDERAL CHARTER AT RISK

California’s latest official assessment results lend context to Shaw’s criticism of Los Angeles Unified’s academic performance. 

In 2025, 46.46% of LAUSD students met or exceeded the state standard in English language arts and 36.76% met or exceeded the standard in mathematics, according to California Department of Education testing data. That meant roughly 53.5% did not meet the ELA standard and 63.2% did not meet the math standard.

Shaw said the criticism described in the video would not change her approach to the statewide race.

"If putting children and families first is a ‘huge problem’ for their agenda, that tells you everything you need to know. I won’t back down," she said. "They just admitted it. I’m a ‘real threat’ to their socialist agenda. Parents over politics. Kids over ideology. Girls over boys in their sports and locker rooms. Keep calling me a threat. I’ll keep being one."

WATCHDOG REPORT EXPOSES TEACHERS UNION 'POLITICAL MACHINE' FUNNELING MORE THAN $1 BILLION TO LIBERAL CAUSES

In the clip, shared by Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation, a woman describes Shaw as a "real threat" and discusses efforts to prevent a "MAGA lady" from taking charge of public education.

The woman then warned about what Shaw taking office would mean for the organization.

"That would cause a huge problem for us," the woman said.

The California Post reported the speaker was Julie Van Winkle, the UTLA AFT vice president.

HOUSE GOP LAUNCHES PROBE INTO 5 MAJOR LABOR UNIONS OVER DEM SPENDING DESPITE MAGA MEMBERSHIP BASE

DeAngelis told Fox News Digital he viewed the purported criticism as evidence that Shaw was threatening teachers unions’ political influence.

"This leaked audio is the best endorsement Sonja Shaw could’ve ever received. When a power-hungry teachers union that fights to protect itself at the expense of kids calls you an existential threat to their socialist agenda, you’re officially over the target," he said.

UTLA has publicly endorsed Shaw’s opponent, San Diego Unified School District Board President Richard Barrera, for California superintendent of public instruction. The union says Barrera has a "proven commitment" to working with educators and families and called for a superintendent who would work with unions on education funding.

Organized labor has also spent millions supporting Barrera. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

California Secretary of State data compiled by CalMatters showed the California Teachers Association Independent Expenditure Committee had spent $5,057,539 supporting Barrera as of Sept. 15, compared with $10,000 in reported outside spending supporting Shaw.

Los Angeles County Republican Party Chair Roxanne Hoge also pointed Fox News Digital to a post from Saturday on X tying the controversy to Gov. Gavin Newsom’s recent overhaul of the superintendent’s authority.

"We knew [Sonja Shaw] was causing good trouble when [Gavin Newsom] stripped the office she's running for of most of its power," she said.

Fox News Digital reached out to UTLA and Newsom's office for comment.

item.title: ‘We beat Disney, Fauci, Soros’: Ron DeSantis unleashes ‘Florida model’ in hard-hitting midterm rally
item.description: Ron DeSantis headlined a rally for Navy veteran Dan Green, a GOP candidate in Florida's 9th district seeking to oust incumbent Darren Soto
item.content:encoded:
Pitching his administration’s conservative record as a national blueprint for Capitol Hill, Gov. Ron DeSantis rallied Republicans in Osceola County Tuesday night, portraying Navy veteran Dan Green’s bid for Florida’s 9th Congressional District as part of a broader push to bring aggressive Florida-style governance to Washington.

Speaking before a crowd in St. Cloud, south of Orlando, DeSantis pointed to his administration's high-profile battles on education policy, state spending reductions and corporate pushback and urged voters to bring that same combative, policy-driven mandate to the halls of Congress.

SOCIAL MEDIA ERUPTS AFTER DESANTIS GIVES ‘SOROS’ PROTESTER A PIECE OF HIS MIND: ‘AIN’T MY FIRST RODEO’

"I will say that I'm looking forward to y'all getting the congressman elected that has served this country and that has served for the right reasons. Now, I am a big believer that we need term limits for members of Congress. But until we do that, you can show your current guy the term limit by kicking him out of office.

"So, I think what we need is what we've done in Florida. It can be a model for people like Dan going to Washington, other states, you name it, because it's not just about peacocking and putting social media press releases out and never getting anything done. We have fought every big fight that there has been to fight in the state of Florida, and we have won every big fight that there is to fight in Florida."

DeSantis rallied the conservative faithful with a recap, alleging major victories over left-wing institutions, agencies and agendas.

"Just think about it. We beat Dr. Fauci on COVID. We beat Disney on gender ideology. We beat Soros on crime by removing two of his prosecutors. We beat Martha's Vineyard on illegal immigration.

"We just beat the Muslim Brotherhood by banning Sharia law. We beat the teachers unions by enacting universal school choice for all Florida families. We beat SEIU by doing paycheck protection.

"Every single time there was a fight, we would beat and win the fights. And that's ultimately what it's all about. Because leadership — when it's popular, when it's easy — anyone can do that. 'I'll just go with the flow,' all this other stuff. It really matters when it is tough and when you're going to face arrows."

TRUMP'S HANDPICKED DESANTIS SUCCESSOR WINS CROWDED GOP PRIMARY FOR FLORIDA GOVERNOR

DeSantis repeatedly emphasized that his top priority was sticking to the courage of his convictions, not seeking political expediency or going along to get along.

"I remember during COVID, I was doing things, and people said, 'Oh, he's not shutting down the beaches. Why does he have these people in school?' And all this other stuff. You know, people come after you, and a lot of people told me that I was frittering away my governorship, that I wouldn't be able to win in '22, and all this other stuff. I don't know if that was true. Who knows, right? 

"But when you get in a position to lead, you either do it or you should just sit down. My job was not to be worried about my own political hide. My job was to be worried about protecting the liberty, jobs, and businesses of the people I was elected to serve. So, we started the fire, and we gave them his right."

It is clear that the two-term governor considers his famed battle with Disney to be a particular feather in his cap.

"Nobody in the history of the state had ever taken on Disney in anything. A lot of people told me I was making a mistake," DeSantis said.

"But the reality is, do we want a society in which our 6-year-olds are being told they can change genders, or do we want a society rooted in truth? If you want a society rooted in truth, even if the biggest, most powerful corporation in the state is against you, you've got to stand up and you've got to fight. And we fought, and we won."

As the federal debt has topped a staggering $40 trillion, DeSantis made the case that he has taken the state on a markedly divergent course.

"Just look at the results. For four straight years, Florida has reduced its budget. Is any other state in the country reducing spending? We've done it four years in a row," DeSantis said.

"I was just able to announce today if you take all of Florida's debt for all of our history up until the time I became governor, just in my tenure, we will retire 54% of the state's debt, more than cutting it in half. 

"We've been ranked No. 1 for education freedom, and our public university system is ranked No. 1. We have the lowest in-state tuition of any state in the United States, and it's the exact same cost today to students and families that it was the day I took office. 

"It did not go up one penny under my tenure. Is there anything else that didn't go up? The dollar menu at McDonald's is all $2.99 now. Everything else has gone up, but that has not gone up."

And DeSantis touts Florida as a national leader in lowering taxes for its citizens and called for voters to back Amendment 3 in Florida, which would pave the way for elimination of non-school property taxes.

"If you look at tax relief, we've done $10 billion over my tenure — more than anyone. Some of it is permanent, like no tax on baby items, back-to-school items and no tax on business rent. But, really, the big enchilada is going to be on the ballot in November when you have a chance on Amendment 3 to vote yourself more control over your own home and not let them tax you to death. So vote yes on 3.

As Republicans face headwinds heading into the midterms in a little over a month, DeSantis drew a parallel between this year's election, and the 2018 election, which propelled him to the governor's mansion by a narrow margin.

"We've done all this stuff, but I think the lesson is this: When I won eight years ago, it was kind of similar to how it is now. People were saying it was a ‘blue year.’ There was a lot of wind in the face of Republican candidates," DeSantis recalled.

"A lot of people thought Florida was a swing state — that we were purple — where one point had decided all these races for the previous decade. A lot of people didn't think I could even win given those circumstances. And even if I won, they said, 'Well, the state's going to go blue. You've got all these people moving from Puerto Rico, the Northeast, anything.' So, I'm running. It wasn't easy, and we won."

DeSantis maintains he has never taken a poll as a means to determine a position on an issue.

"It was a close race, so I had a choice to make: Do I try to tiptoe around the tulips, not offend anybody, and just try to walk this tight line? Or do I say, 'You know what? I won the election. I got 100% of the executive power, and I didn't get elected to follow. I got elected to lead,'" DeSantis said.

"So, I am going to fly the banner of bold colors, not pale pastels. I'm going to do what I believe in. I am not going to take any polls. I have not to this day ever polled a single issue in my entire time as governor.

"The reason is simple. … It depends on how you ask the question, right? I can tweak the words and get a different result. But also, what does a poll actually mean? Like Popeye said, ‘I am what I am,’ right?"

item.title: Phillies force Game 3 as Kyle Schwarber, Bryce Harper go back-to-back and Alec Bohm homers in 10th vs Braves
item.description: Alec Bohm's 10th-inning home run forced a decisive Game 3 after Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper launched back-to-back blasts to erase a deficit.
item.content:encoded:
Game 2 of the National League Wild Card Series was deadlocked at 3-3 Wednesday afternoon before Alec Bohm delivered Philadelphia's biggest swing. His two-out homer in the 10th inning lifted the Phillies to a 4-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves and forced a winner-take-all Game 3.

The Phillies had trailed 3-1 before Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper hit back-to-back homers in the seventh. Harper's blast came one inning after he committed a costly fielding error.

Andrew Painter then took over. The regular-season starter worked three scoreless innings to protect Philadelphia's taxed bullpen, stranded two runners in the 10th and struck out Dominic Smith after the Phillies won an ABS challenge.

MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL DESPERATELY NEEDS TO FIX ITS TERRIBLE POSTSEASON SCHEDULING PRACTICES

Playing under traditional extra-inning rules that don't include designated runners at second base like in the regular season, Bohm delivered his third career postseason home run, a 357-foot shot to right field off right-hander Didier Fuentes.

The Phillies will try to continue their postseason dominance over the Braves in Thursday's Game 3. Philadelphia beat Atlanta in the 1993 NLCS and the 2022 and 2023 NLDS.

In the seventh, Drake Baldwin's double glanced off Harper's glove in right field, driving in Sean Murphy to give Atlanta a 2-1 lead. Harper, who resumed playing the outfield late this season for the first time since 2022, got a poor jump and was leaping for the ball near the warning track. He was not charged with an error. Matt Olson added a sacrifice fly.

"Probably should have been caught, obviously," Harper said.

The Phillies pulled even with eighth-inning home runs by Schwarber and Harper off Dylan Lee, the winning pitcher in the Braves' 5-3 opening win on Tuesday. Schwarber’s drive carried 447 feet and Harper followed with a 418-foot drive.

item.title: Fetal tissue supplier billed $765 procurement fee per organ, warns records could imply illegal sales: records
item.description: Records obtained by David Daleiden’s Center for Medical Progress show UCLA purchase orders tied $765 procurement service fees to individual liver and thymus specimens
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Newly obtained public records show Cercle Allocation Services billed a UCLA research operation a $765 procurement service fee tied to each individual liver and thymus specimen, while warning in internal correspondence that certain billing language could improperly imply the tissue itself was being sold.

The records, obtained from UCLA through a California Public Records Act request made on behalf of Center for Medical Progress founder David Daleiden, include purchase orders and correspondence between the university and Cercle Allocation Services.

An internal UCLA order form identifies the purchasing operation as part of the David Geffen School of Medicine’s Division of Hematology-Oncology and references the "Mouse Core." UCLA redacted the names and other identifying information of researchers from the record.

The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that UCLA or its researchers, procurement personnel or other employees engaged in illegal or unethical conduct with the transactions.

'DRUG-DEALING' NETWORK SHIELDED BY BLUE STATES TARGETED IN SCOTUS CHALLENGE

One UCLA purchase order lists seven individually numbered liver and thymus specimens at a $765 unit amount apiece, totaling $5,355. Another lists five specimens from Aug. 18, 2023, each carrying the same $765 amount, for a total of $3,825. Additional purchase orders reflect the same per-specimen amount.

Cercle objected to the purchase orders’ tax treatment and asked UCLA to reissue them, telling the university that the charges reflected procurement services and that sales tax should not be applied. Cercle said tax language could improperly imply that the specimens themselves were being sold.

Cercle does supply human fetal tissue for biomedical research. Peer-reviewed scientific literature has identified the company as the source of human fetal liver tissue used by researchers, providing independent evidence of the type of procurement business described by CMP.

SUPREME COURT UNANIMOUSLY SLAPS DOWN BLUE STATE TARGETING PRO-LIFE GROUP

CMP identified the liver and thymus specimens in the UCLA purchase orders as fetal tissue. Fox News Digital has not independently verified that the tissue associated with these specific purchase orders was fetal. The purchase orders identify the organs by type, sample number and date but do not describe them as fetal.

The records do not establish that the payments were illegal. Cercle characterized the money as fees for procurement services rather than payments for the tissue itself.

But correspondence shows the company was particularly concerned about how those payments were described.

"The overriding issue is the use of terminology that we must not use due to their improper implication that we are selling taxable items, which we are not," a Cercle accounts manager wrote in September 2023. "Due to the nature of our business, we must be very careful and clear that we invoice fees for our procurement services."

The same email said notations referring to sales tax would imply Cercle was "selling the items received," which the company said were "illegal to sell." Cercle instead instructed UCLA that purchase orders should authorize payment for its services while tying individual sample numbers and dates to a unit amount of $765.

The correspondence shows UCLA subsequently prepared revised purchase orders after Cercle objected to the tax language.

One Cercle email said a July invoice totaling $5,355 for procurements on three dates had already been "processed and paid." The company also asked UCLA to replace other purchase orders containing tax language, including one covering five procurements from Aug. 18 worth a combined $3,825.

Federal law prohibits knowingly acquiring, receiving or otherwise transferring human fetal tissue for "valuable consideration," if the transfer affects interstate commerce, while allowing "reasonable payments" associated with transportation, implantation, processing, preservation, quality control or storage.

The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that Cercle or UCLA violated that prohibition.

Daleiden contends the documents raise questions about whether the uniform $765 charges represented permissible reimbursement for procurement-related costs.

HAWLEY SENDS CRIMINAL REFERRAL OF 'LEFT-WING DARK-MONEY' GROUP OVER MAILED ABORTION DRUGS

He pointed to the uniform $765 amount UCLA assigned to individual specimens on the purchase orders, including multiple organs listed on the same date. Daleiden told Fox News Digital he believes the structure raises questions about whether the payments reflected the procurement-related costs permitted under federal law.

Documents reviewed by Fox News Digital do not contain Cercle’s invoices or underlying cost calculations and do not establish whether the $765 amount exceeded reasonable procurement-related expenses.

Daleiden also said UCLA did not produce Cercle’s invoices in response to the public records request.

The May 2025 request sought the original and most recent materials associated with UCLA IRB No. 11-002504 and records and communications from 2023 forward between the authors of a specified UCLA study and Advanced Bioscience Resources or Cercle. The request covered records, including emails, text messages, notes and fetal tissue logs.

UCLA later said its departments had completed their search and that the September 2026 production represented the final batch of non-exempt responsive records. The university said it redacted certain researcher identities because of concerns about threats and harassment involving sensitive research.

Records also show the UCLA-Cercle relationship continued into 2025.

A February 2025 Cercle ticket involving UCLA was titled "Liver and brain." Cercle responded March 3 that it had been "unable to fulfill your request today" and canceled the ticket. The records do not specify that the requested tissue was fetal or establish that any brain tissue was ultimately procured or transferred.

Daleiden has spent years investigating fetal tissue procurement after CMP released undercover videos involving Planned Parenthood officials in 2015. His recording operation later became the subject of a California criminal case.

Kamala Harris’ office opened the investigation while she was California attorney general. Charges were later filed under Attorney General Xavier Becerra. In April 2026, a California judge dismissed the final charge and expunged the case.

The records reviewed by Fox News Digital do not establish that the UCLA-Cercle transactions violated federal law. UCLA and Cercle have not been accused or charged by authorities with illegal conduct in the transactions reflected in the public records obtained by CMP.

UCLA and Cercle Allocation Services did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: WNBA commentator Sydney Colson physically restrained after going after Fever fan following A'ja Wilson mess
item.description: Video footage captures Sydney Colson lunging at a spectator as an Amazon staffer physically restrains her during a WNBA playoff game Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Former Indiana Fever player and Amazon Prime commentator Sydney Colson lost complete control during Tuesday’s WNBA playoff game between the Las Vegas Aces and Fever, lunging at a spectator while a staff member physically restrained her.

The chaos began when Aces star A’ja Wilson overreacted to a fan who simply pointed at her and shouted, "It’s on you!" following a foul call. Wilson marched two rows deep into the baseline seats to confront him, earning a technical foul for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Instead of maintaining professional distance as a credentialed media member, Colson and fellow Amazon analyst Theresa Plaisance (also a podcast co-host with Wilson) left their courtside seats and inserted themselves into the altercation.

As arena personnel escorted Colson and Plaisance away from the baseline, a spectator in a red Fever shirt directed a comment toward them. Plaisance pointed back and called him a "little b***h boy." Colson then continued pushing aggressively toward the fan as an Amazon staffer struggled to hold her back. Video footage captured her shouting, "Who do you think you are? B—-, who the f— do you think you are?"

Colson spent the 2025 season in Indiana before exiting the franchise. Ever since packing her bags, taking public cheap shots at her former team has become a habit.

Right on script, the broadcast team immediately scrambled to run cover for Wilson.

Prime Video analyst LaChina Robinson insisted on-air that "something was said" simply because Wilson does not normally react that way.

Aces coach Becky Hammon predictably chimed in, claiming she had never seen Wilson react like that and assuming her star felt "deeply disrespected."

Wilson doubled down after the game, apologizing to her teammates for picking up the technical foul while insisting the fan’s conduct crossed the line.

"I don’t know if you guys know me, but I don’t get into the bulls—," Wilson told reporters. "I try to play my game, keep it pushing. But if I’m just walking, because I just got the foul, I’m chilling, and if I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said. I don’t give a damn how you said it. The tone, that is unacceptable."

Wilson went further, complaining about how the fan was allowed to return to his seat after security reviewed the incident.

"And how he gets back in the game because they said he didn’t do anything? Of course he did, and that’s fine," she said.

The Fever confirmed that arena security interviewed witnesses and found zero violations of the Fan Code of Conduct.

In August, after Chicago’s DiJonai Carrington was ejected for a dangerous neck hit on Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, Colson publicly targeted her former teammate by sarcastically posting, "Love a trans foul," on social media.

In any other professional sports league, a credentialed commentator physically restrained from charging a paying fan would face immediate suspension or termination.

Yet Colson remained mic’d up for Amazon’s broadcast during the entire outburst, while the live coverage rushed to defend Wilson without acknowledging that the fan broke zero rules.

Don’t hold your breath waiting for Amazon or WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert to do anything about it.
